text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock gained 7.6% over two weeks and added another 0.12% today in a narrow move. The company operates in an exceptionally tight refining environment right now: U.S. refineries are running at 98% capacity, and diesel inventories have fallen to just 104 million barrels while geopolitical disruptions—Ukraine hitting Russian refineries and Iran-U.S. military escalation—are pushing diesel to record highs. This creates a favorable margin environment for U.S. refiners like Marathon, which can process crude into high-priced products at full throttle.

The broader momentum reflects sustained oil market tension. U.S. crude has gained over 9% this week as military exchanges between Washington and Tehran continue, and the EU's formal entry into Iran sanctions this week narrows global refining capacity further. With storage at these levels and demand still intact, refiners face weeks or months of wide profit spreads before the situation normalizes.
